candidate.description: A supplied OLE DOC can encode increasing contiguous logical CP ranges while repeatedly pointing each piece.fc at the same small valid WordDocument byte range. main_text verifies logical continuity (1154-1174) and each source offset (1188-1202), but neither total logical characters nor repeated source consumption. It appends one StoryChar per logical CP (1221); Fib::parse trusts attacker ccp_text from the FIB (925), up to u32::MAX. A small source range reused by a modest piece table can request billions of StoryChar records, exhausting caller memory before DOCX admission.
candidate.reachability: public legacy_doc::read (180-189), doc_to_docx (235-236); CLI run_convert_any reads and dispatches OLE to doc_to_docx (src/bin/jubarte.rs:3125-3131) before any admit_word, whose later branch explicitly excludes legacy (3142-3143). Even read_document's refusal-hint path invokes legacy_doc::read before returning error (2742-2753).
candidate.prerequisites: Victim processes attacker-supplied legacy DOC through convert/public legacy reader (or CLI rejection hint). Structurally readable OLE/FIB and contiguous CP piece table with valid reused source extents, without encryption.
candidate.counterevidence: OLE FAT/mini-FAT chains bounded by input sectors; source offsets checked; pieces cover ccp_text and nondecreasing. They do not bind logical output to source bytes. Caller CPU/memory isolation limits impact to process DoS.
